question: Does deleting EU Article16 prohibit independent national information duties, and do these five records establish more than a literal difference?
shortAnswer: No: deletion by itself does not establish that every independent national information duty is unlawful. A coherent narrower case concerns retention of the identical automatic EU collection scheme, especially where made a market-entry condition or officially identified as needing repeal. National-only duties surviving a deliberate partial repeal require additional proof of impediment, disproportionality or pre-emption; that proof is not currently established.

framework.assessment: Article6(1) protects market access for compliant marked equipment with declaration. Article9 restricts protective market measures to non-compliance with EU requirements. Article14(3) preserves reasoned documentation requests. Article17 saves proportionate rules on equipment use/person protection, not a blanket all-type data-collection exemption. Those safeguards support scrutiny of a new market-entry condition; they do not automatically prove any postmarket national copy is forbidden.

coherentDistinction: Retain an additional premarket formality contrary to a specific free-movement guarantee (PT), or an expressly recognised pending repeal of the identical EU scheme (AT, more cautiouslyFI), while withdrawing deliberately preserved national-only information duties whose independent legality has not been resolved (HU/LV). Neither endpoint rests solely on whether the paragraph text matches. If recognised reform tracking is not enough for this catalogue, AT/FI should also be withdrawn pending stronger legal-result proof; PT remains materially distinct.
